rationale.conceptual: An established but non-trivial method: DFT interface calculations with amorphization via ReaxFF, Bader charge analysis, and work of adhesion. Requires understanding of plane-wave DFT, k-points, pseudopotentials, and charge analysis, but no novel algorithm or deep research-grade derivation.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: ReaxFF MD amorphization (LAMMPS), DFT geometry optimization (Quantum ESPRESSO), Bader analysis, and bond extraction. Requires installing multiple scientific codes, obtaining force fields and crystal structures, and managing intermediate file handoffs. Several fragile dependencies and non-trivial orchestration.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires reproducing DFT-based interface calculations for HA and Si-doped HA on TiO2. Conceptual difficulty is moderate (standard DFT workflow with amorphization and doping, but well-documented). Execution is challenging due to a multi-stage pipeline spanning classical MD (ReaxFF), DFT (Quantum ESPRESSO), and post-processing, with fragile tooling and data assembly. Resources are modest: tiny models, CPU-only DFT.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small interface models (~114 atoms) make DFT feasible on a single CPU node with moderate RAM; no GPU required. Input structures are kB-scale.
